traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Gentianaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple, lamina entire; Lucid key (read 2026-10-17): no lobing.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Gentianaceae (read 2026-10-17): simple symmetric blades, lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, oblanceolate, obovate or oblong. Ranking ours, weighted by Gentiana (over 300 species, Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17)), Gentianella and Swertia, whose stem leaves are mostly lance-shaped.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409: stamens 4 to 5, up to 12, as many as the corolla lobes.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409: corolla sympetalous, rotate to salverform.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 293 Gentianaceae: annual or perennial herbs, very rarely woody; leaves opposite, entire, often joined at the base; no stipules; flowers regular, mostly showy and bright; corolla united, of 4 to 12 lobes; stamens as many as the lobes, on the corolla; ovary superior, mostly of one cell with two placentas on its wall (two carpels); fruit mostly a capsule. Simple leaves from 'entire', read as undivided.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 410, family Gentianaceae: inflorescence cyme, raceme or solitary, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 409, 410, family Gentianaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite, usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.
